title: Want to Lose Weight? Listen to Yourself Eat

image.attribution: Musée du Cacao et du Chocolat / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-2.0

main_content:
Restaurant chefs, home cooks, and foodies – people who love good food – often say that we eat with all of our senses.

First, we use our sense of sight to appreciate how a meal is presented. Our sense of touch can also be important.

Next, with our sense of smell, we breathe in the aromas. Finally, we enjoy the food with our sense of taste.

But what about our sense of hearing? Does sound also affect our dining experience?

A new report answers, ‘yes,’ it does.

That answer comes from researchers at Brigham Young University and Colorado State University in the United States. They found that hearing is important in the eating experience.

Hearing is often called “the forgotten food sense,” says Ryan Elder.

Elder is an assistant professor of marketing at Brigham Young University’s Marriott School of Management. He says that if people notice the sound the food makes as they eat it, they might eat less.

Elder says that when hiding the sounds of eating, like when you watch television or listen to loud music, we take away the sense of hearing. And this may cause you to eat more than you would normally.

questions.question: Who are foodies?
options: People who only eat fast food
Individuals passionate about cooking and enjoying food
People who dislike experimenting with new cuisines
questions.answer: Individuals passionate about cooking and enjoying food

questions.question: What did the researchers at Brigham Young University and Colorado State University say about hearing?
options: Hearing is not relevant to the eating experience
Hearing is important and can influence how much we eat
Hearing is the least effective sense in dining
Hearing impacts food preparation techniques primarily
questions.answer: Hearing is important and can influence how much we eat

questions.question: What can take away the sense of hearing?
options: Focusing on the flavors of the food
Watching television or listening to loud music
questions.answer: Watching television or listening to loud music
